result:
The proposed answer of 12 is wrong because it includes the paw and the diamond, and both contain a triangle.

Take H = K₃. A subdivision of K₃ is any cycle, so C_{K₃} is the class of chordal graphs. Split graphs are chordal and have unbounded clique-width (Golumbic–Rotics), so C_{K₃} has unbounded clique-width. The paw and the diamond each contain K₃ as an induced subgraph. Any subdivision of either still contains an induced cycle, which is an induced subdivision of K₃, so C_{K₃} ⊆ C_paw and C_{K₃} ⊆ C_diamond. Since a subclass of a bounded clique-width class is bounded, unbounded C_{K₃} forces C_paw and C_diamond to be unbounded too. Neither can be in 𝓜.

The sufficiency argument for the paw and the diamond therefore cannot be correct. The killing argument for the triangle is also missing. The stated list of survivors is inconsistent with this, so the final set 𝓜 = {P₄, paw, diamond} and the sum 12 cannot be right. I did not determine the correct 𝓜 or its edge-count sum.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
